name: Shaphan
overview: Shaphan is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Jaazaniah, as recorded in Ezekiel 8:11. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him in Scripture. His mention is brief but establishes a familial connection within the prophetic narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaphan means 'rock badger' in Hebrew, according to Ezekiel 8:11. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects a common Hebrew personal name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shaphan as the father of Jaazaniah, based on Ezekiel 8:11. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shaphan's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as the father of Jaazaniah, who is mentioned in a vision describing idolatrous practices in Jerusalem. This connection places Shaphan within the context of the spiritual challenges faced by the people of Judah during the prophetic ministry of Ezekiel. While Shaphan himself is not a central figure, his mention contributes to the historical and relational framework of the passage.
